chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Thaqafi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying: In the case of a man who claimed against a woman that he married her with a guardian and witnesses, and the woman denied this, then the sister of this woman brought evidence against another man that he married her with a guardian and witnesses, and they did not specify a time. 'Indeed, the evidence is the husband's evidence, and the woman's evidence is not accepted because the husband has already acquired the right to the intimacy of this woman, and her sister wants the dissolution of the marriage, so her claim is not verified and her evidence is not accepted unless there is a specified time before her time or consummation with her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a wife's sister's testimony to be accepted in dissolving a marriage when the husband claims it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in Shia jurisprudence, where the husband's established right to conjugal relations (*istihqaq al-budh*) takes precedence over the wife's desire to dissolve the marriage. It specifies that the sister's testimony is only admissible if it proves a distinct time of marriage prior to the husband's claim or confirms consummation, thereby preventing arbitrary annulment. This ruling underscores the evidentiary burden placed on the party seeking to overturn an existing legal status.
